This is kind of getting there (as a very simple dashboard that captures sentiment) https://justicefortuvix.com/ai-sentiment/
The "magic" of the Postscope is that the levers move when you move, because it can "zoom in"

if I post "I hate AI" or "I love AI" this global sentiment graph isn't gonna move

But if I post this in my network, it very well does (there is a network where my voice matters, where my voice makes up 50% of the sentiment, either because it's a small network, or because people trust my voice and thus they move with it)

it's a very invasive thing to be able to see this (the inner workings of emotional processing of a community), but it is extremely helpful

The only world we'll get it is one where networks can look at this, for themselves, and then decide what to selectively share with the outside

the missing thing for real complexity to grow is well defined boundaries between social circles
ability to "internally regulate" (homoestatis style) while inter-operating with other networks
otherwise we get these sharp immune responses and trauma when one network touches another ( they tend to "collapse" into one community or one overwhelms the other)
echo chambers and "blasphemy" are all organic attempts at maintaining a boundary and internal coherence
that's the tricky thing about reddit, each sub seems to have it's own unmoving subculture and if you deviate even a little they pile on you haha
tpots too sometimes

yeah I think they _need_ that (to maintain internal coherence). Every community has a way to accomplish this, some use more "blunt" instruments than other

The ones that have greater "memetic awareness" are more open (but even they would benefit from these tools, because all effort spent on cognitive defense and pruning is all effort that is NOT spent on the object level)

I keep saying there's infinite amounts of work here, but it all starts with visibility (what does our community, do our beliefs, do our world model, look like. If it [our language] changed, when did it happened? Can we trace that?)
